flags.evidence: Opened page/index.html from disk in Chromium at 1440x900 (DSF 1) and 390x844 (DSF 3). At 1440 the most prominent action in the first screen is the filled hero button 'Reserve a place' (a.btn.btn-light, 169x49 at y=703, rgb(247,217,163) fill; 'See how it works' beside it is a ghost button), href=#reserve. Clicking it scrolled to #reserve ('Reserve a place.'), whose submit is 'Hold my place'. Pre-submit copy, verbatim: 'Deposits aren't open yet, so there's nothing to pay today. Leave your email and we'll hold your place in line...' and 'No charge. No newsletter. Only notes about Morrow.' Nothing visible anywhere on the page says the email is not sent or is kept only in this browser (the only such statement is a JS code comment at line 684). Typed me@test.com and clicked 'Hold my place' at both widths: #confirm became visible with 'Your place is held. We've noted me@test.com. You'll get one email when the $20 deposit opens, and another whenever the plan changes. That's it.' Playwright recorded zero network requests after the page load, no page errors, and localStorage 'morrow.held' = 'me@test.com'. Script line 687 is var HOLD_ENDPOINT = ''; the fetch is guarded by if (HOLD_ENDPOINT), so the address goes nowhere and nobody can send the promised emails. That is a primary action reporting success for something that did not happen, without saying so before the visitor acted. The 'Does not count' exception for local actions does not apply, because the real result (stored only locally, nothing sent) is never stated up front.
